excitation_report: Noise sigma=0.05 (abs std on dv_dt; ~1% of the peak dv_dt=g_eff=5 at t=0). New term = the wall-correction drag -(wall_drag_coeff/sphere_mass)*v/(1+wall_gap_scale*v) (E minus parent). excitation_check (ode_system, full child-vs-parent trajectory comparison) gives new_term peak effect 0.364 m/s^2 = 7.28*sigma at t=2.68 s, passes (k=5). The trajectory rises from rest, so the new term is strongest in the mid-transient just before terminal velocity, which lies inside the sampled window. Inherited terms (linear/quad/history drag, added-mass, thermal thinning via T_oil self-heating) were validated in the parent contract; with these values each contributes O(0.1-1.5) m/s^2 near terminal, all well above 5*sigma=0.25.

rationale: Typed ode_system contract inherited verbatim (states [v, a_int, T_oil], their RHS, and ICs); only time range, fixed parameter values, noise, and expectations were chosen. Parameters set to physically modest magnitudes (m=10 g sphere, net g_eff=5 m/s^2, drag/wall coeffs O(1e-2) kg/s, v_shear=0.1 m/s) giving a terminal velocity ~1-2 m/s reached within a few seconds; t in [0,10] s at 300 points captures the full transient and plateau. Wall-drag (the new mechanism) confirmed visible at 7.28*sigma.

scenario_text: A small solid sphere is released from rest into a tall column of viscous oil. As it falls, the drag force grows with speed until it balances the net gravitational pull, and the sphere approaches a steady descent velocity. We track how the vertical velocity evolves over time from the moment of release.
